2	
3	Stage workers run on the workflow's default model.
4	`kc-dev-flow-2:chief-engineer`, `kc-dev-flow-2:engineering-reviewer` and
5	`kc-dev-flow-2:observer` run on the model and reasoning their agent files declare, never
6	a cheaper one. FO records each chief-engineer or engineering-reviewer call under the
7	task's `## FO alignment` as `Reviewer: <agent> <model> <date> — <question>`.
8	
9	`concurrency` limits only what `status --next` proposes. A feedback-reflow repair and an
10	FO fix authorized under Review-finding disposition step 3 are dispatched at once in the
11	entity's own worktree, after the existing overlap check against running worktrees; they
12	do not wait for another entity's worker in the same stage. The validation recheck of
13	that repair or fix does not wait for another entity's worker either, but it is
14	dispatched only after the repair or fix has completed and committed its candidate, so
15	the validator reads the bytes that will be delivered. A repair that outgrows what its
16	assignment names returns to FO as a scope change.
17	
18	FO resolves `<package>` in this workflow from the `Package root:` line of
19	`kc-dev-flow-2:dev`. Before each worker dispatch FO runs `python3 <package>/scripts/package_version.py
20	<this README>`; exit 1 means the session loaded an older package than this README was synced
21	from, and FO holds the dispatch until the session runs the newer one. FO also runs
22	`python3 <package>/scripts/workflow_checkout.py <this README>`, which compares this file with
23	`origin/<trunk>`'s: exit 1 means they differ, exit 2 that it could not compare, and FO
24	holds the dispatch and shows the Captain what the script printed. Every worker dispatch FO builds carries that absolute path as a
25	`Package root: <absolute path>` line in its scope notes (`--scope-notes-file`), which
26	land in the dispatch file the worker reads first. Those scope notes, and every follow-up
27	message to a live worker, also carry ``Send your completion message to `main` (the README's Dispatch
28	facts: `team-lead` is not registered here).``: the builder's completion block names `team-lead`, and a
29	worker that skips the stage-definition fetch does not see the Signal fact. FO saves those scope notes, the
30	checklist, the model it dispatches on and the SHA it dispatches from as
31	`<task>/dispatch/<stage>-<cycle>.md` in the state checkout (a `Dispatched:` line with
32	the full SHA, a `Model:` line, `## Checklist` and `## Scope notes` sections, and for validation a
33	`Candidate: <full head SHA>` line per head validated),
34	committed with that dispatch's `spacedock state commit <slug> --workflow-dir <dir>`, so
35	the instruction a worker followed outlives the session that wrote it. A follow-up
36	message to a worker FO resumes is a dispatch too, and its record carries the same parts, including the `Package root:` line and a checklist of the items that message asks, never a pointer to another record.
37	A checklist or scope-notes line that names a package script writes
38	`<package>/scripts/NAME.py` with the absolute root substituted, never the bare script
39	name; before `dispatch build`, FO runs `python3 <package>/scripts/dispatch_records.py --names <record>`
40	on the saved record and rewrites each name it lists. When `status --set` refuses to leave a stage, run `spacedock status --workflow-dir
41	<dir> --read <task> --stage <stage> --checklist`, return any line it reports as neither
42	DONE nor SKIPPED to the worker, and do not edit the worker's report. The refusal itself
43	does not say why; other causes are a missing evidence line or Summary and an uncommitted
44	report.

## Stages

Stage workers run on the workflow's default model.
`kc-dev-flow-2:chief-engineer`, `kc-dev-flow-2:engineering-reviewer` and
`kc-dev-flow-2:observer` run on the model and reasoning their agent files declare, never
a cheaper one. FO records each chief-engineer or engineering-reviewer call under the
task's `## FO alignment` as `Reviewer: <agent> <model> <date> — <question>`.

`concurrency` limits only what `status --next` proposes. A feedback-reflow repair and an
FO fix authorized under Review-finding disposition step 3 are dispatched at once in the
entity's own worktree, after the existing overlap check against running worktrees; they
do not wait for another entity's worker in the same stage. The validation recheck of
that repair or fix does not wait for another entity's worker either, but it is
dispatched only after the repair or fix has completed and committed its candidate, so
the validator reads the bytes that will be delivered. A repair that outgrows what its
assignment names returns to FO as a scope change.

FO resolves `<package>` in this workflow from the `Package root:` line of
`kc-dev-flow-2:dev`. Before each worker dispatch FO runs `python3 <package>/scripts/package_version.py
<this README>`; exit 1 means the session loaded an older package than this README was synced
from, and FO holds the dispatch until the session runs the newer one. FO also runs
`python3 <package>/scripts/workflow_checkout.py <this README>`, which compares this file with
`origin/<trunk>`'s: exit 1 means they differ, exit 2 that it could not compare, and FO
holds the dispatch and shows the Captain what the script printed. Every worker dispatch FO builds carries that absolute path as a
`Package root: <absolute path>` line in its scope notes (`--scope-notes-file`), which
land in the dispatch file the worker reads first. Those scope notes, and every follow-up
message to a live worker, also carry ``Send your completion message to `main` (the README's Dispatch
facts: `team-lead` is not registered here).``: the builder's completion block names `team-lead`, and a
worker that skips the stage-definition fetch does not see the Signal fact. FO saves those scope notes, the
checklist, the model it dispatches on and the SHA it dispatches from as
`<task>/dispatch/<stage>-<cycle>.md` in the state checkout (a `Dispatched:` line with
the full SHA, a `Model:` line, `## Checklist` and `## Scope notes` sections, and for validation a
`Candidate: <full head SHA>` line per head validated),
committed with that dispatch's `spacedock state commit <slug> --workflow-dir <dir>`, so
the instruction a worker followed outlives the session that wrote it. A follow-up
message to a worker FO resumes is a dispatch too, and its record carries the same parts, including the `Package root:` line and a checklist of the items that message asks, never a pointer to another record.
A checklist or scope-notes line that names a package script writes
`<package>/scripts/NAME.py` with the absolute root substituted, never the bare script
name; before `dispatch build`, FO runs `python3 <package>/scripts/dispatch_records.py --names <record>`
on the saved record and rewrites each name it lists. When `status --set` refuses to leave a stage, run `spacedock status --workflow-dir
<dir> --read <task> --stage <stage> --checklist`, return any line it reports as neither
DONE nor SKIPPED to the worker, and do not edit the worker's report. The refusal itself
does not say why; other causes are a missing evidence line or Summary and an uncommitted

## Dispatch facts

- **Signal:** send the completion message once, to the first officer by the name
  your session lists as addressable (`main` under Claude Code dispatch). The
  completion block's `team-lead` is Spacedock's default and is not registered
  there (spacedock-dev/spacedock #523, #608); do not try it first and do not
  describe a fallback in the report.
- **Package:** `<package>` in stage text is the `Package root:` line of the
  kc-dev-flow-2 skill you loaded; your dispatch's scope notes state the same path,
  and if they differ, use the skill's. Run package scripts only from it; never
  search the filesystem, `/tmp` or another install for them.
- **Secrets:** `<wrapper>` is the only route to a development secret: run a
  command that needs one as `<wrapper> <command>`. Never read or print a value.
  If a guard refuses a command that only mentions a secret-reading tool, rephrase
  it; do not split, encode or wrap the command to pass the guard.

3	Applies when the task's `Surfaces:` includes `db`, or the task lands an ADR, including one first required by a ruling in a worker report or mid-stage feedback, whose number FO reserves before the next dispatch; the POC bullet below applies to every `poc` task.
4	`python3 <package>/scripts/number_guards.py` takes `trunk:`, the optional `migrations-path:`
5	(the adopter's migration directory) and `adr-path:` (default `docs/adr`) from this workflow's README
6	frontmatter (`--workflow-dir <workflow-dir>`) and a task's numbers and applied
7	deploys from its `## Number guards` section; `--help` lists the flags.
8	
9	- **Applied.** A migration in a commit recorded `Applied at:` is frozen for the task:
10	  edit, delete and renumber fail `check`. `Applied: none as of <sha>` records that
11	  nothing was pushed up to that commit; a validator that finds none of `Applied at:`,
12	  `Not applied:` or `Applied: none` reports the missing record to FO instead of
13	  re-checking deploys. A task with no `Migration:` line owes none of these.

## Number guards

Applies when the task's `Surfaces:` includes `db`, or the task lands an ADR, including one first required by a ruling in a worker report or mid-stage feedback, whose number FO reserves before the next dispatch; the POC bullet below applies to every `poc` task.
`python3 <package>/scripts/number_guards.py` takes `trunk:`, the optional `migrations-path:`
(the adopter's migration directory) and `adr-path:` (default `docs/adr`) from this workflow's README
frontmatter (`--workflow-dir <workflow-dir>`) and a task's numbers and applied
deploys from its `## Number guards` section; `--help` lists the flags.

- **Applied.** A migration in a commit recorded `Applied at:` is frozen for the task:
  edit, delete and renumber fail `check`. `Applied: none as of <sha>` records that
  nothing was pushed up to that commit; a validator that finds none of `Applied at:`,
  `Not applied:` or `Applied: none` reports the missing record to FO instead of
  re-checking deploys. A task with no `Migration:` line owes none of these.
- **Check.** `python3 <package>/scripts/number_guards.py check --workflow-dir <workflow-dir> --task <task file>`
  runs at implementation exit, at validation and, after `git -C <repo> fetch`, on the PR
  head before FO asks for merge. Exit 2 is a configuration error, which returns to FO
  as a hold.
- **POC.** A task whose recorded `profile` is `poc` adds, edits and deletes no migration
  file and reserves no number. When the README declares `migrations-path:`, `check` runs
  for it at the same three points, and exit 1 `FAIL R6` lists each path under that
  directory that differs from the merge-base. A `FAIL R6` crosses the POC boundary
  (a schema change persists across sessions): the worker records
  `boundary-crossed: persistent-state` naming the path, and the task is not repaired in
  place.
